summary: Cycle patching converts a successor assignment into one TSP tour by swapping successors across disjoint cycles.
description: Input is a finite complete cost matrix and a valid successor permutation. Output is one open tour. The separate decomposition function identifies the cycles of the assignment.

Choose the cross-cycle swap with the smallest cost increase and recompute cycles until only one remains. This direct greedy patching uses at most cubic time, may break a low-cost assignment and makes no optimality claim.
